dimensions.name: responsibility-ownership
dimensions.evidence: C1-C12 and U1-U6 assign backend history to unisim, task-specific terms/config to UniLab, generic env lifecycle to ManagerBasedRlEnv, and learner/IPC/checkpoint state to uni_rl.

dimensions.name: public-interface
dimensions.evidence: The plan requires a public SimBackend history contract and explicitly forbids private MuJoCo access from the env layer.

dimensions.name: dependency-direction
dimensions.evidence: The map preserves unisim backend APIs -> UniLab EnvProtocol/task composition -> uni_rl runtime injection without copying IPC into UniLab.

dimensions.name: state-lifecycle
dimensions.evidence: Terminal next-state identity, four-sample history order, learner-only discriminator/replay/normalizer mutation, and checkpoint compatibility are explicit migration risks.

dimensions.name: change-surface
dimensions.evidence: The work is split into owner-scoped U1-U4 units, with offline/runtime closure in U5 and distillation isolated in U6.

dimensions.name: evidence-boundary
dimensions.evidence: The map limits its claim to ownership and scope and expressly excludes module, runtime, training, and policy-quality proof.

dimensions.name: tensor-provenance
dimensions.evidence: The frozen inventory binds 195D state, 390D transition, N/T/feature axes, float32 representation, device transfer, terminal substitution, validity, and finite-value behavior.

dimensions.name: gradient-update-boundary
dimensions.evidence: The inventory freezes D_k scoring before actor/critic update, detached discriminator reward scoring, and learner-only discriminator mutation before D_(k+1).

dimensions.name: persistence-evaluation
dimensions.evidence: Checkpoint schema and replay/normalizer/discriminator persistence are assigned to uni_rl, while legacy compatibility remains an explicit U4 decision and training quality remains out of scope.

evidence.observation: The revised map binds repository URLs, release commits, detached read-only checkouts, and installed-package source equivalence.
